summary: Path join/normalise/confine library on caller-provided buffers (both '/' and '\\' separate segments). v1 keeps '..' segments in the normalised result, guards only against the literal spelling '../' and checks containment with a raw string prefix, so a client path such as '..\\..\\etc\\passwd' or a sibling directory named '/srv/data-old' escapes the root (path traversal, CWE-22); v2 resolves '..' with a bounded segment stack, rejects climbing above the top, and requires a whole-segment prefix; v3 is a behaviour-preserving refactor of v2; v2c lowers the segment-stack depth constant.

pairs.intent: CWE-22 fix: pn_normalize resolves '..' against the preceding segment (bounded stack, new pn_segment_is_dotdot helper) and fails with PN_ERR_ESCAPE when it would climb above the top; pn_is_under compares whole segments; pn_resolve stops relying on the blacklist helper pn_looks_unsafe, which is removed.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-22: only "." and empty segments were dropped; ".." survived into the result. v2 pops the previous segment (stack of 16) and returns PN_ERR_ESCAPE for a ".." with nothing to pop.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-22: bare string prefix, so "/srv/data-old/x" counted as under "/srv/data"; v2 also requires the next character to be a separator or the end of the path.
